title: NY State Assembly · District 63
area: Staten Island's West Shore and North Shore, including Port Richmond, Mariners Harbor, Bulls Head, Travis and Westerleigh.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled. Incumbent Samuel Pirozzolo advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries unopposed; Matthew Mobilia advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. This is a rematch of the 2024 general election, which Pirozzolo won 57.3%-42.2%.

summary.text: Samuel Pirozzolo is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent seeking a third term. A native Staten Islander and small-business owner, he has focused his first term on opposing battery-energy-storage sites, congestion pricing and bail reform, and on property-tax and education issues.

background.text: Born in and lives in New York, New York (Staten Island); career experience includes working in his family's optical practice for more than three decades.
Served as president of Community Education Council 31 on Staten Island for seven years and as Vice President of the New York City Parents Union.
Elected to the New York State Assembly on November 8, 2022, to represent Staten Island's West Shore.
Assigned in 2025-2026 to the Children and Families, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Energy, and Higher Education committees.

priorities.text: Opposes the siting and construction of battery energy storage systems in the district, citing fire and safety risks.
Opposes congestion pricing, green-energy mandates and other policies he says raise energy bills, tolls and taxes for working families.
Wants the city's property-tax assessment system updated, saying Staten Island's single- and two-family homes are taxed at higher effective rates than larger multifamily buildings.
Supports repealing cashless bail reform and backs the NYPD.
Says he has delivered funding for Staten Island schools, nonprofits and substance-abuse treatment providers.

positions.summary: Opposes congestion pricing, describing it as one of several policies driving up costs for Staten Island families.
positions.quote: He opposes congestion pricing schemes, green energy mandates that spike your utility bill, and tax hikes disguised as investments.

positions.summary: Opposes green-energy mandates that he says raise utility bills, as part of opposing what his campaign calls the cost-of-living agenda coming out of Albany.
positions.quote: green energy mandates that spike your utility bill

record.text: Prime-sponsored A00139, which would prohibit siting or construction of battery energy storage systems in Assembly District 63; held for consideration in the Local Governments Committee on May 20, 2025.

Prime-sponsored A09019, which would prohibit the New York City mayor from residing in a rent-stabilized apartment and authorize a landlord to bring an eviction proceeding against the mayor; held for consideration in the Housing Committee 17-8 on May 20, 2026.
Prime-sponsored A00263, a constitutional amendment to lengthen Assembly and Senate terms to six years and impose term limits on legislators; referred to the Governmental Operations Committee.

Prime-sponsored A08927, which would prohibit cannabis retail licensees from operating a storefront within 500 feet of child day-care centers, public parks or playgrounds; referred to the Economic Development Committee.
Voted no on S10113 (cannabis microbusiness showcase-event permits), which passed the Assembly 88-53 on June 5, 2026.
Voted no on S3460 (grants employees access to their personnel records), which passed the Assembly 92-49 on May 19, 2026.

candidates.name: Matthew Mobilia
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after it was canceled; ran unsuccessfully against Pirozzolo in 2024.

summary.text: Matthew Mobilia is a Staten Island trial attorney and former Richmond County prosecutor running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Samuel Pirozzolo for the second consecutive election.

background.text: Born and raised in Staten Island; earned a B.A. in politics from Saint Anselm College and a J.D. from Albany Law School (2015).
Worked as a New York City prosecutor in the Richmond County District Attorney's Office under DA Michael E. McMahon, trying cases including homicides, burglaries, DWI and narcotics offenses.
Served as an Associate Court Attorney to Judge Matthew P. Blum of Kings County Civil Court, handling no-fault, landlord-tenant and civil litigation.
Founded The Law Office of Matthew Mobilia PLLC in 2022, a Staten Island practice handling criminal defense, personal injury and real estate matters.

priorities.text: Public safety: stronger community policing, better law-enforcement training, and collaborative initiatives with community leaders.
Local economy: financial support and reduced regulation for small businesses to revitalize the local economy.
Neighborhoods: investing in local infrastructure, public services and educational initiatives.
Human and civil rights: opposing discrimination and injustice and promoting equal treatment.

candidates.researchNotes: Mobilia has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has never held elected office, so there is no official record. His campaign site states four broad priority areas but does not take specific positions matching this guide's fixed issue list; none are included rather than inferred from party or general statements.
